question.problem:
Find the radius of convergence $R$ and interval of convergence $I$ for the series

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(x-1)^{2n-1}}{2n-1}\,.
$$
question.worked_solution:
To apply the ratio test, we define ${a}_{n}=\frac{(x-1)^{2n-1}}{2n-1}.$ Then, we calculate the ratio of two successive terms and take the limit as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{(x-1)^{2(n+1)-1}}{2(n+1)-1}\cdot \frac{2n-1}{(x-1)^{2n-1}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{(x-1)^{2n+1}}{2n+1}\cdot \frac{2n-1}{(x-1)^{2n-1}}| \\  & =|x-1{|}^{2}{lim}_{n\to \infty }(\frac{2n-1}{2n+1}) \\  & =|x-1{|}^{2}{lim}_{n\to \infty }(\frac{(2-\frac{1}{n})}{(2+\frac{1}{n})}) \\  & =|x-1{|}^{2}\cdot \frac{2}{2} \\  & =|x-1{|}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges if $L<1.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}|x-1{|}^{2} & <1 \\ |x-1| & <1 \\ -1<x-1 & <1 \\ 0<x & <2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the radius of convergence is $R=1,$ and the series converges for any $x$ that lies in the open interval $(0,2).$

The ratio test gives no conclusion about the convergence of the series when $L=1.$ So, when $|x-1|=1,$ we do not know if the series converges. This means that the endpoints $x=0$ and $x=2$ need to be investigated separately using another test for convergence.

- When $x=0$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(x-1)^{2n-1}}{2n-1} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{((0)-1)^{2n-1}}{2n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{2n-1}}{2n-1} \\  & =-1-\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{5}-⋯ \\  & =-(1+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{5}+⋯)\end{aligned}
$$

Comparing the above series in parentheses with ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{n},$ we see that the series is divergent by the limit comparison test.

- When $x=2$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(x-1)^{2n-1}}{2n-1} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{((2)-1)^{2n-1}}{2n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(1)^{2n-1}}{2n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2n-1} \\  & =1+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{5}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Comparing the above series with ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{n},$ we see that the series is divergent by the limit comparison test.

So the interval of convergence is $I=(0,2).$
